### Observed differences

- Three activities all but disappeared: in the earlier window A19, A20 and A25 each took part in about 31–37% of traces (roughly 62–73 of 200 traces each), while in the later window A19 appears in only 1 of 200 traces and A20 and A25 in none. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- In the earlier window these three behaved as alternatives rather than a sequence: each pair occurred together in only about 1% of traces, while exactly one of them ran in about 30–36% of traces. [REL001, REL003, REL008]
- Earlier, about 86 in 100 of A41's observed outgoing transitions led into this block (to A25 about 32%, A19 about 29%, A20 about 26%); in the later window about 86 in 100 lead directly to A26. [DIR005]
- Earlier, each block activity led overwhelmingly to A26 (about 94–97% of its observed outgoing transitions); in the later window A20 and A25 show no observed outgoing transitions, and A19's single observation points to A12. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR004]
- The gap from A41 to A26 shortened: earlier it was typically 2 event positions (about 85 in 100 cases, with 3 positions in about 15); in the later window it is typically 1 position (about 86 in 100). [LAG001]
- Relations with the surrounding activities changed accordingly: earlier A19, A20 or A25 co-occurred with A26 or A31 in about 31–37% of traces, always before them, and A41 preceded them in about 31–37%; in the later window A26, A31 and A41 occur in essentially all traces (99–100 in 100) without any of the three. [REL004, REL005, REL006, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL013, REL014, REL015]
- A21's outgoing transitions shifted shares: A24 rose from about 14% to about 35% of A21's observed outgoing transitions, while A31 fell from about 54% to about 38%. [DIR003]
- A26's mean position moved slightly earlier (about 0.39 to 0.37 of the trace) and A41's slightly later (about 0.32 to 0.33); these small shifts are consistent with the block's disappearance rather than independent findings. [POS004, POS005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the alternative block of activities A19, A20 and A25, which used to run between A41 and A26, is no longer executed in the later window, so that A41 now flows directly to A26. Earlier, about one third of traces contained exactly one of the three, A41 fed into the block in about 86% of its outgoing transitions, the block led on to A26 in about 95% of cases, and A26 typically followed A41 two positions later; in the later window the three activities appear in 0–1 of 200 traces, A41 points to A26 in about 86% of its outgoing transitions, and the A41–A26 gap is typically one position. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR005, LAG001, REL004, REL009, REL013]

The screening produced 29 qualifying items against roughly 0.57 expected if nothing had changed, so the ensemble is unlikely for a stable process, and the participating items — the participation collapse, the redirection of A41, the shortened A41–A26 lag and the changed relations — all describe one coordinated structural difference. Because the activities are nearly absent in the later window, this is a removal or bypass of a block, not a shift of shares between surviving paths. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR005, LAG001]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the block remains in the process but was not triggered in any of the 200 later traces; zero participation only means the activities were not observed, and the later outgoing profile of A19 rests on a single trace. [OCC002, OCC003, DIR001]

Other differences: A21's outgoing transitions redistributed, with A24 rising from about 14% to about 35% and A31 falling from about 54% to about 38% of its observed outgoing transitions; this may be a downstream consequence of the same change, but the evidence does not link it directly to the block's removal. [DIR003]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Screening: 114 units tested, 29 items qualified, 0.57 expected without change. 29 items is many times larger than 0.57, so the count cannot be explained by chance as a whole. So we go beyond the screening comparison and judge by directness, consistency, and ability to rule out competing explanations.

All evidence is control-flow family (OCC, DIR, POS, REL, LAG). No time items (TWAIT), no resource items (ASSIGN, CONC, HAND). So I must not discuss time or resources.

Let me look at the evidence:

OCC001: A19 participation 0.365 → 0.005 (73 traces before, 1 after). Decreased.
OCC002: A20 participation 0.31 → 0.0 (62 before, 0 after). Decreased.
OCC003: A25 participation 0.35 → 0.0 (70 before, 0 after). Decreased.

So three activities A19, A20, A25 were each present in roughly 31–37% of traces before, and essentially absent after (1 trace for A19, 0 for A20 and A25).

DIR001: A19's outgoing transitions: before mostly A26 (94.5%), after only A12 (100%, but support after = 1 trace). So A19 nearly disappeared; the after profile is based on 1 trace only.
DIR002: A20's outgoing: before mostly A26 (96.8%), after empty (0 traces).
DIR004: A25's outgoing: before mostly A26 (95.7%), after empty (0 traces).

DIR003: A21's outgoing redistributed: before A31 53.5%, A23 28.9%, A24 14.0%; after A31 37.6%, A24 34.7%, A23 24.8%. Support 114 before, 101 after. Observed change 0.094, empirical strength 0.995. This is a modest redistribution: A24 up from ~14% to ~35%, A31 down from ~54% to ~38%.

DIR005: A41's outgoing: before spread across A19 (29%), A25 (31.5%), A20 (26%), A08, A10, A06, etc.; after mostly A26 (85.6%). Support 200 before, 202 after. So A41 previously led to A19/A20/A25 (the three activities that disappeared) about 86% of the time; after, it leads to A26 about 86% of the time. This is consistent with A41 now bypassing the A19/A20/A25 block and going directly to A26.

POS001-003: A19, A20, A25 positions — support collapsed, consistent with disappearance. POS004: A26 position shifted slightly earlier (mean 0.390 → 0.372), support 200 both. POS005: A41 position shifted slightly later (mean 0.317 → 0.333), support 200 both.

REL items:
REL001 (A19,A20): before, A_only 35.5%, B_only 30%, cooccurrence 1%, neither 33.5%; after neither 99.5%. So both disappeared.
REL003 (A19,A25): similar.
REL008 (A20,A25): similar.
REL002 (A19,A24): before cooccurrence 17%, A_before_B 16.5%, B_only 32.5%; after B_only 55.5%, neither 44%. So A19 gone, A24 remains.
REL007 (A20,A24): similar.
REL012 (A24,A25): before B_before_A 17.5% (A25 before A24), A_only 32%, B_only 17.5%, neither 33%; after A_only 56%, neither 44%. So A25 gone, A24 remains.
REL004 (A19,A26): before cooccurrence 36.5% (A19 before A26 35%), B_only 63.5%; after B_only 99.5%. So A19 used to precede A26 in ~35% of traces; now A26 always occurs without A19.
REL005 (A19,A31): similar — A19 before A31 in 36% before; after A31 always without A19.
REL006 (A19,A41): before B_before_A 36.5% (A41 before A19); after B_only 99.5%. So A41 used to precede A19 in 36.5% of traces; now A41 occurs without A19.
REL009 (A20,A26): A20 before A26 in 30% before; after A26 always without A20.
REL010 (A20,A31): A20 before A31 in 30.5% before; after A31 without A20.
REL011 (A20,A41): A41 before A20 in 31% before; after A41 without A20.
REL013 (A25,A26): A25 before A26 in 35% before; after A26 without A25.
REL014 (A25,A31): A25 before A31 in 35% before; after A31 without A25.
REL015 (A25,A41): A41 before A25 in 35% before; after A41 without A25.

LAG001 (A41,A26): before, gap of 2 steps in 84.5%, 3 steps in 15%; after, gap of 1 step in 85.8%, 2 steps in 13.4%. So the distance from A41 to A26 shrank from typically 2 steps to typically 1 step. This directly supports that the block between A41 and A26 (containing A19/A20/A25) was removed/bypassed — A41 now leads directly to A26.

So the picture: In the earlier window, A41 was followed (in ~86% of traces) by one of A19, A20, A25 (each ~26–32%), which in turn was followed by A26 (and sometimes A31). In the later window, A19, A20, A25 essentially disappeared (0–1 traces out of 200), and A41 now leads directly to A26 (~86%), with the A41→A26 gap shrinking from 2 steps to 1 step.

This is a coherent hypothesis: a group of activities (A19, A20, A25 — apparently alternatives, since REL001/REL003/REL008 show they rarely co-occur: cooccurrence ~1% or less, A_only/B_only patterns) that used to sit between A41 and A26 was removed or is no longer executed; A41 now bypasses directly to A26.

Wait — are A19, A20, A25 alternatives? REL001 (A19,A20): before cooccurrence 0.01, A_only 0.355, B_only 0.30, neither 0.335. So they rarely co-occur — they're alternatives (each in ~31-37% of traces, together in ~1%). REL003 (A19,A25): cooccurrence 0.005. REL008 (A20,A25): cooccurrence 0.01. Yes, they are alternatives: exactly one of the three typically executes.

And each of them was followed by A26 (DIR001: A19→A26 94.5%; DIR002: A20→A26 96.8%; DIR004: A25→A26 95.7%). And A41 preceded them (DIR005 before: A41→A19 29%, A41→A25 31.5%, A41→A20 26%).

Also A26 and A31: REL004/005 show A19 before A26 and A19 before A31 each ~35-36% — hmm, A19 before A26 in 35% and A19 before A31 in 36%? That suggests after A19, both A26 and A31 occur (A19 cooccurs with A26 36.5% and with A31 36.5%). So after the alternative block, both A26 and A31 follow. DIR003 shows A21→A31 53.5%, A21→A23 28.9%, A21→A24 14% before; after A31 37.6%, A24 34.7%, A23 24.8%. A21 is a different activity though.

The main hypothesis: the alternative block {A19, A20, A25} between A41 and A26 was removed (activities became skipped/no longer executed), so A41 now flows directly to A26. Supporting signs:

- A19/A20/A25 were alternatives (rarely co-occurring) [REL001, REL003, REL008].

Competing explanations: Could this be a shift in path frequencies (existing paths taken with different frequencies)? No — the activities are (nearly) absent in the later window, which per the instructions indicates activities were removed/became optional/skipped, not a shift in shares between alternatives. The condition for "path frequency shift" requires every activity observed in substantial share in both windows — not the case here.

Could it be sampling variation? 29 items vs 0.57 expected — no, far too many. And the items are consistent, telling one coherent story.

Is this "Supported hypothesis" or "Weak hypothesis"? The evidence is direct and consistent: participation collapse (OCC), redirection of A41 (DIR005), lag shrinkage (LAG001), and relational changes (REL). The DIR005 and LAG001 items have full support (200/200, 202/202). The hypothesis is directly shown: A41 previously led into the alternative block, now leads directly to A26. I'd say "Supported hypothesis" — the evidence supports it directly and consistently. The screening count (29 vs 0.57) rules out chance as a whole.

Limitations: we cannot tell whether the activities were removed from the model or just not executed in these 200 traces (zero participation only means not observed); also DIR001's after-profile rests on a single trace. Also POS004/POS005: A26 slightly earlier, A41 slightly later — but these are consequences of the same structural change (position shift alone doesn't show movement; and they're minor).
